![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/559548dc5f2570d1341760ab87a2619646ed6985fd6437cb29442dc58bc6fee4.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x={y}^{2}+2y-1$ and $x=-1-{y}^{2}$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $x=-2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+2y-1 & =-1-{y}^{2} \\ 2{y}^{2}+2y & =0 \\ 2y(y+1) & =0 \\ y & =-1,0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=-1$ to $y=0.$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/8f1bccafe64a6926bdb214410453cecafa7059f74a539b155a4a4e6cccd67d1a.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x={y}^{2}+2y-1,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=-1-{y}^{2}.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=-1-{y}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/7d1d1ed82fadf105997e00d39b99992cdeba1d41be13cf599db63b34902e149a.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[\,(-1-{y}^{2})-(-2)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[1-{y}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x={y}^{2}+2y-1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/040e0a87b4bb5c7121a27fd2cc94c520f76919afbb86a49cfed2ed0cf57c1561.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[\,({y}^{2}+2y-1)-(-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[{y}^{2}+2y-1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[{y}^{2}+2y+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[1-{y}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[{y}^{2}+2y+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({[1-{y}^{2}]}^{2}-{[(y+1)^{2}]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({(1-{y}^{2})}^{2}-(y+1)^{4})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
